title: Safe Calculator
story: Your calculator app crashes every time someone divides by zero. Instead of crashing, you want it to say "Cannot divide by zero!" Enums can carry either a success value OR an error message — no crashes needed.
why: Enums let functions return success OR failure in a single type, so callers must handle both cases.
analogy: A CalcResult is like a package from a store. You either got what you ordered (Value) or received a notice saying "out of stock" (Error). You don't know which until you open it.
try_it: Add a `safe_modulo(a: Int, b: Int) -> CalcResult` function that returns the remainder of a / b, or an error if b is 0. Add a `safe_power(base: Int, exp: Int) -> CalcResult` that errors if exp is negative. Chain three operations: divide 10 by 3, get the value, then modulo that value by 2.
tips: Return `Error(...)` early when you detect a problem — no need to wrap everything in else
Every caller MUST match on the result — the compiler ensures you handle both success and failure
Name your variants clearly: `Value`/`Error` or `Ok`/`Err` — consistency helps readers
common_mistakes: Only matching on `Value` and ignoring `Error` — if a variant isn't matched, the code won't compile
Using `if` instead of `match` to check results — this often misses the error case
